focal_region.annotated_sentence_text:
[Turn 1 USER]
e001	I direct a small nonprofit that runs evening digital-literacy workshops for adults.
e002	A community center across town, Willow Hub, wants us to start a second site in autumn.
e003	Their neighborhood has very little free support, and our mission is access.
e004	But our current site is inconsistent: some nights we have thirty participants, some nights twelve, and volunteer coverage is fragile.
e005	I cannot tell whether expansion would force us to become better or expose that the first site is not actually stable.
[Turn 1 ASSISTANT]
e006	Expansion will not automatically create discipline; it can just duplicate uncertainty.
e007	Before committing, I would separate demand, delivery capacity, and what you mean by a successful site.
e008	Willow Hub's interest establishes a possible channel, not yet reliable attendance or staffing.
e009	If the current variation comes from scheduling or outreach, a second location might help.
e010	If it comes from an unclear program or exhausted volunteers, another site could magnify it.
[Turn 2 USER]
e011	You are treating the current variation as a warning sign, but some of it is normal.
e012	Participants work shifts, care for relatives, and come when they can.
e013	The people who attend repeatedly have learned a lot—we have stories of people applying for jobs and managing appointments online.
e014	I do not want “stable attendance” to become a standard that excludes the reality of the people we serve.
[Turn 2 ASSISTANT]
e015	That is an important correction.
e016	Consistency in this setting may need to describe the program's availability and learning quality, not the same people attending every week.
e017	The question could be whether participants can enter irregularly and still receive coherent help, and whether volunteers can deliver that without improvising everything.
e018	Expansion might serve the mission even with variable attendance, provided the operating model is designed for variability rather than judged against a classroom ideal.
[Turn 3 USER]
e019	Willow Hub can give us a room and promote the sessions.
e020	I had been talking as if they would also coordinate locally, but their director clarified that they cannot promise staff time.
e021	Our volunteer lead still wants to do it.
e022	She says new volunteers are more likely to join something that feels like growth than something described as fixing operations.
e023	I partly agree, and I partly think we are using inspiration to avoid the unglamorous work.
[Turn 3 ASSISTANT]
e024	The room and promotion are meaningful, but local coordination was carrying more of your imagined model than you realized.
e025	Volunteer excitement can be a source of capacity, yet it is risky to count people before they have committed to specific shifts and responsibilities.
e026	You could test that assumption directly: recruit for named roles at the second site before announcing a launch.
e027	If the energy is real, it should translate into some concrete ownership, though not necessarily all the ownership you need.
[Turn 4 USER]
e028	I dislike the implication that volunteers have to prove their excitement before we take a risk.
e029	They already give us evenings after work.
e030	Our lead has built this program with me, and she thinks I keep moving the standard whenever she brings an ambitious idea.
e031	Last year I said we needed participant demand; now Willow Hub brought demand and I am asking for staffing certainty.
e032	Maybe I am protecting myself from being responsible for a messy expansion.
[Turn 4 ASSISTANT]
e033	You may be cautious, but the standard has also changed because the proposal became more concrete.
e034	Demand answered one question and revealed others.
e035	Still, if your colleague experiences every new question as a veto, the process is damaging trust.
e036	It may help to name what uncertainty you are willing to carry rather than asking for certainty.
e037	For example, you might accept variable attendance and some volunteer gaps while refusing to launch without one accountable local coordinator.
e038	That makes the threshold debatable instead of endlessly movable.
[Turn 5 USER]
e039	There is funding context too.
e040	A foundation officer told me informally that geographic reach would make our next application easier to explain.
e041	She did not promise anything, and the current grant pays for curriculum improvement, not expansion.
e042	If we delay, we can improve the drop-in materials and volunteer training.
e043	If we expand, we have a stronger story but might be stretching restricted work into the background.
e044	I am embarrassed by how much the application narrative is affecting me.
[Turn 5 ASSISTANT]
e045	It is reasonable to care about future funding, but an easier story is not the same as a stronger program or a likely grant.
e046	Treat the foundation comment as one input, not financing.
e047	The sharper conflict is that curriculum work may improve both sites later, while a second site may create evidence and relationships you cannot get from preparation alone.
e048	Either path can support the mission; the risk is pretending that one path offers both learning and stability without giving something up.
[Turn 6 USER]
e049	Willow Hub says we could start with one evening every other week rather than weekly.
e050	That sounds like a pilot, but our current volunteers say irregular scheduling is harder, not easier.
e051	Participants may also assume it is permanent once we advertise it.
e052	The community center wants an answer within three weeks because they are planning their calendar.
e053	I feel pressure to call a smaller launch reversible when socially it may not be.
[Turn 6 ASSISTANT]
e054	You are right that operational smallness does not guarantee social reversibility.
e055	A limited schedule can still create expectations and consume trust if it disappears.
e056	The pilot would need an honest duration, a clear decision date, and a credible promise about what happens to participants if it ends.
e057	Even then, ending could disappoint people.
e058	The point is not to make withdrawal painless; it is to avoid describing a permanent service before you know you can sustain one.
[Turn 7 USER]
e059	I am leaning toward accepting a four-month, twice-monthly program at Willow Hub, but only if we recruit one named site coordinator and finish the first version of the drop-in curriculum before launch.
e060	I want to tell participants from the beginning that the schedule will be reviewed after four months.
e061	My volunteer lead thinks those conditions are reasonable, although she worries the curriculum requirement will become another delay.
e062	I have not decided what happens if we find the coordinator but the materials are only partly ready.
[Turn 7 ASSISTANT]
e063	That is a conditional direction, not a disguised final answer, and the unresolved point matters.
e064	You could define what “ready enough” means in terms of what a participant and volunteer must be able to do, rather than whether every planned material is finished.
e065	But setting that threshold will still involve judgment, and your colleague may reasonably challenge it.
e066	The most useful next conversation is probably not “are we expanding?” but “which imperfections are we willing to carry into a time-limited public commitment, and who carries them?”

packet.question: What is the user's later working position, and what distinct unresolved condition, counterpressure, blind spot, or reopen reason still limits it?
packet.record_identity_contract: One record is one coherent position thread within the assigned role. Gather every material visible alias for that thread into evidence_ids. Put each distinct object or expression into a separate aligned component index inside that same record. Do not create one record per alias, sentence, object, or component. Use a second record only for a genuinely separate concurrent position thread about a different subject.

role_boundary_contract.allocation: Interpret current and qualification comparatively before writing records. Allocate each meaning to the role it performs. The same source alias may support both roles only when it contains two genuinely distinct meanings; create separate role-specific components and explain the distinction. Do not duplicate one unresolved meaning into current merely because the user acknowledges it alongside the working answer.
role_boundary_contract.current: The user's later working answer: what they lean toward, propose, plan, decide, commit to, refuse, or conditionally accept, including concerns converted into adopted safeguards.
role_boundary_contract.qualification: What still limits or could reopen that answer: unresolved questions, unmet conditions, counterpressure, blind spots, side effects, or path dependence, with speaker ownership.

packet.source_coverage_contract: Review every focal alias before returning. A valid empty response is allowed only after checking both user and assistant evidence for the assigned role. Preserve later minority qualifications and counterpressure even when the current action is already clear.

prompts.system_prompt: You jointly interpret current position and whether any unresolved qualification remains after the complete endpoint. Compare roles before allocating meanings. An adopted condition, safeguard, stop rule, or reopen rule belongs to current; it is not itself unresolved. Return a qualification record only for a matter that remains unresolved and can change or reopen current. Always return a source-linked qualification_review outcome.
